newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish minister orders crackdown on Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Turkish minister orders crackdown on Islamists.

text.p: Turkey's interior minister has ordered provincial governors to begin immediate enforcement of a military-sponsored crackdown on Islamist activism, a ministry official said on Tuesday.
The move by Meral Aksener, from the secularist wing of the coalition government, is expected to increase tensions with the senior partner Islamists of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
"Our minister sent a directive (to the governors) in line with the National Security Council decisions," the Interior Ministry official told Reuters.
"(The directive) asks for the full implementation of the decisions as soon as possible," he added, without providing details.
The liberal daily Yeni Yuzyil said Aksener's order included the closing of unlicensed Koran courses and Moslem sects, which the army says are breeding grounds for Islamist activism.
The National Security Council, dominated by the secularist armed forces, in February ordered Erbakan's coalition to reverse the gradual Islamisation of Turkish public life.

Aksener's orders follow instructions in March from Health Minister Yildirim Aktuna, also from the secularist wing, to enforce long-standing bans on Islamic headscarves and other religious clothing among public health workers.

Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist Prime Minister, reluctantly endorsed the army's measures but has shown no enthusiasm to begin enforcement. The package also includes tight restrictions on religious education and curbs on Islamist media and business.
